key_insight: A ternary-solvent growth strategy produces hybrid perovskite monolayers exceeding 1000 µm², enabling lithography-free optoelectronics with ultra-low static power.
engineering_relevance: Large, isolated ultrathin channels support solvent-free shadow-mask contacts, reducing fabrication-related chemical damage and standby power.
method: Combine alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive to suppress out-of-plane stacking.
Control precursor solvation and edge-mediated transport during annealing.
Fabricate planar devices using physical shadow masks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports approximately 0.2 pW static power at 5 V, a 250-fold reduction versus drop-cast films, and a light-to-dark current ratio of 4.3 × 10².
watch_item: Wafer-scale uniformity, device yield, and operational stability remain unestablished in the abstract; no AI method or solar-cell efficiency is reported.
paper_title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
